q: Why are the price and hash-rate charts drawn on a logarithmic scale?
options: Their values span many orders of magnitude, so a linear axis would hide the early years
Logarithmic scales make prices look higher
rationales: A log axis changes spacing, not values; it hides nothing and exaggerates nothing.
The API returns plain values; the scale is a drawing choice.

q: 20,087,925 bitcoins are in circulation. About what share of the 21 million cap is that?
rationales: Half the cap was issued back in 2012; far more has been issued since.
About 912,000 bitcoins remain, over four per cent of the cap.

q: Why does yearly issuance drop in steps rather than smoothly?
options: The block subsidy halves every 210,000 blocks
rationales: No vote exists; the schedule is fixed by the protocol.
Issuance follows the schedule regardless of demand.

q: How is the network hash rate obtained?
options: Estimated from mining difficulty and block times
rationales: No node can see other miners' hashes; only found blocks are visible.
Miners do not report their hashing; it would be unverifiable anyway.
